chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْكَرْخِيِّ قَالَ:

translations.en: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ الضَّيْعَةُ الْكَبِيرَةُ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْمِهْرَجَانِ وَ النَّيْرُوزِ أَهْدَوْا إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْءَ لَيْسَ هُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ يَتَقَرَّبُونَ بِذَلِكَ الشَّيْءِ إِلَيْهِ

translations.en: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who owns a large estate, and when the day of al-Mihrajan and al-Nayruz comes, they give him something as a gift; it is not something owed by them, but they seek nearness to him through that thing.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ «أَ لَيْسَ هُمْ مُصَلِّينَ» قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ «فَلْيَقْبَلْ هَدِيَّتَهُمْ وَ لْيُكَافِهِمْ».

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "Are they not people who perform salat (prayer)?" I said: "Yes." He عليه السلام said: "Then let him accept their gift and reciprocate them."

en.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on accepting gifts given on customary festive occasions such as al-Mihrajan and al-Nayruz. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that if the givers are Muslims and the gift is not an unlawful due, then accepting it and reciprocating it is permissible.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to accept and reciprocate gifts given on cultural festivals like Nayruz?

key_terms.الضَّيْعَةُ: a landed estate or agricultural property
key_terms.الْمِهْرَجَانِ: the festival of Mihrajan, a seasonal cultural celebration
key_terms.النَّيْرُوزِ: Nayruz, a known cultural festival day
key_terms.مُصَلِّينَ: people who perform salat (prayer), indicating Muslim identity
key_terms.وَ لْيُكَافِهِمْ: and let him reciprocate them in return
